summary: The Aizawa (Langford) system with its usual constants, integrated with RK4 and scaled to fit.

claims.claim: dx/dt = (z − b)x − dy, dy/dt = dx + (z − b)y, dz/dt = c + az − z³/3 − (x² + y²)(1 + ez) + fzx³, with a = 0.95, b = 0.7, c = 0.6, d = 3.5, e = 0.25, f = 0.1.
claims.how: The recipe's flow function is the system's three equations with the published constants; a test compares it term by term.

sources.title: Strange attractors: the Aizawa attractor
sources.says: Parameters a = 0.95, b = 0.7, c = 0.6, d = 3.5, e = 0.25, f = 0.1; also called the Langford system, after W. F. Langford's 1984 numerical studies of torus bifurcations.

claims.test: tests/mt2.spec.mjs: each attractor's equations are the published ones

claims.claim: The path and the tracers are integrated with the classic fourth-order Runge–Kutta method, at fixed steps, so a tracer moves the same at any frame rate.
claims.how: rk4() takes the four classic slopes; the tracers step a fixed h in the system's time, carrying the remainder between frames.

sources.title: Runge–Kutta methods
sources.says: The classic fourth-order method (RK4) takes four slope evaluations per step; its total error falls as the fourth power of the step.

claims.test: tests/mt2.spec.mjs: RK4 is fourth order; the tracers move the same at any frame rate

claims.claim: A tracer dropped off the attractor is pulled onto it.
claims.how: The tracer starts at the tapped point and simply follows the flow; nothing steers it.

sources.title: Strange attractors: the Aizawa attractor
sources.says: Parameters a = 0.95, b = 0.7, c = 0.6, d = 3.5, e = 0.25, f = 0.1; also called the Langford system, after W. F. Langford's 1984 numerical studies of torus bifurcations.

claims.test: tests/mt2.spec.mjs: a tap drops a tracer where it lands
claims.note: Points very far out are kept within a little more than the attractor's box first, so they can be seen.

simplified: The tracers' speed is chosen so the heads move at an easy pace.
The long path is one solution of 110 time units after a settling run.
